plan: My private value is $15. In a first-price sealed bid auction, the optimal strategy is typically to bid slightly less than my true value. Since I want to maximize potential profit, I'll bid close to my value but not exactly at it. This gives me a chance to win if others bid lower, while protecting some potential profit margin. I'll bid $14.5, which is just below my true value, hoping to win if others bid conservatively.

My private value is $36. In a second-price sealed bid auction, the optimal strategy is typically to bid my true value. Since the second-highest bid determines my payment, I want to win if my value exceeds other bids. By bidding $36, I maximize my chance of winning while ensuring I only pay less than my bid. This strategy minimizes overpaying and maximizes potential profit.

My private value is $42. In a second-price sealed bid auction, the optimal strategy is typically to bid my true value. This ensures I win if the item is worth more to me than others, and I only pay the second-highest bid. Since values are drawn independently and randomly, I can't predict others' values. Bidding exactly $42 maximizes my potential profit by ensuring I win if my value is highest while minimizing overpayment.
